key_insight: Recurrent neural networks trained for free recall can develop multiple, human-like memory strategies—not just one classical temporal-context mechanism. The best-performing models use an index-based approach that resembles the memory palace technique.
problem_solved: This paper addresses how to model free recall in a way that captures the diversity of strategies people may use, instead of assuming memory relies on a single temporal context process.
method: Train recurrent neural networks to perform free recall tasks.
Compare the learned internal strategies against classical temporal context models and human recall patterns.
Analyze top-performing models to identify whether they use temporal, index-based, or other memory mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that neural systems can discover multiple valid algorithmic solutions to memory tasks when optimized end-to-end. It suggests more flexible, strategy-diverse models may better match human cognition and improve memory-related AI systems.

paper_title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
paper_authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar
